notes:
Summary: Cascade HelpOps is a mid-enterprise contact center platform (SaaS) powering ~4k agent seats for several telco + retail customers. They're evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace current in-house LLM routing/assist stack. Primary drivers: predictable latency under spikes, cost control for 24/7 usage, and strict data residency/SOC2 requirements.

Requirements / constraints (voice of customer):
- Must support sustained bursts (5k-10k concurrent inference requests) and occasional spikes up to 50k RPS for short windows (marketing events / outages).
- Hard SLA targets: p95 <= 150ms for agent-assist path, tail latency mitigation for tool-calls that invoke CRMs.
- Isolation: tenant-level data separation, VPC endpoints, ability to run private control plane for sensitive accounts.
- Audit & keys: KMS integration, audit logging retention 7 years for regulated customers.
- Tool-calling: need native function/tool calling to orchestrate actions in agent desktop (create ticket, pull account history). Prefer small JSON outputs and structured tool responses.
- Model preferences: open-model family (Llama/Onnx/Redwood-verified variants) with quantization options; fallback to cheaper small models for non-critical reranking.

POC learnings / quotes: "Batching and KV caching reduced per-token latency by ~30% on our workload" — engineering lead.  Marco noted: "Edge-case: session affinity for agents with long chats; KV cache warm-up was key."

Open items: procurement sign-off timeline; legal data-residency language (EU customers); run 72-hour soak test for sustained concurrency; confirm canary rollout + automatic fallback policy for model degradations.

Next tactical steps: get final SOW with residency appendix, schedule 72h soak (SE + infra), procurement to review pricing band, CISO to sign off on KMS diagram.
